creator: Couch Investor
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; auto-captions garble names/numbers in places
summary: Couch Investor's self-described 'therapy session' on a broad AI/growth selloff day. He argues the market remains headline-driven: delayed OpenAI/Anthropic IPOs and a hotter CPI print — driven mostly by fuel, oil and gasoline, with core readings only slightly hot — knocked names down without changing fundamentals, and portfolios having a strong year are simply giving some back. The core segment examines CoreWeave's spiking bond yields (2032s around 14.3%, 2031s around 15.7%, quarterly interest heading toward $900–950M) as a trust problem around delivering data centres and paying interest on time, while Oracle's rising yields are less concerning given its profitable core; CoreWeave's CEO blames rivals' IPO delays bleeding into its narrative. He then rebuts Paul Tudor Jones's renewed '1999, challenging 2027' call — the same comparison as a year ago, in a market now funded by trillion-dollar companies generating huge free cash flow — while conceding 2027 risks (capex growth slowing, inflation, recession, more hikes, three possible $2T IPOs draining flows). ASML's strong earnings and raised margin outlook (stock down ~2% anyway) illustrate demand outstripping supply into 2028–30. Calls: AXON BUY (reiterated, no price), NBIS CONDITIONAL_BUY — Nebius down ~10%, he adds if it dips back under $200; AVGO, CRWV, ORCL and ASML are UNCERTAIN mentions. Auto-captions garble several names ('Nebus', 'Entropic', 'Tudtor Jones').
